title: A Catfish Hatches Inside a Mother Fish's Mouth and Eats Her Eggs

scenes.text: This mother fish is guarding her babies' killers.
scenes.keywords: mouthbrooding cichlid female mouth full of eggs

scenes.text: Lake Tanganyika cichlids carry their eggs in their mouths for six to seven days.
But as she spawns, a cuckoo catfish darts in and drops its own eggs within seconds.
She scoops up everything. The catfish eggs hatch first, in two to four days.
scenes.keywords: cichlid picking up eggs fish eggs macro

scenes.text: Inside her mouth, the catfish fry eat her unhatched eggs, one by one.
It's the only fish on Earth known to do this. And she keeps guarding them for weeks. Her babies' killers.

description:
The cuckoo catfish of Lake Tanganyika is the only fish known to be a brood parasite. It drops its eggs among a mouthbrooding cichlid's eggs while she spawns; she gathers them into her mouth, the catfish hatch first and eat her eggs and fry inside.
First described in Nature in 1986; a 2018 Science Advances study found Tanganyika cichlids have learned to reject catfish eggs far better than naive cichlids from other lakes.
Which animal is the most ruthless parent-cheat you know?
thumbnail_text: BORN IN HER MOUTH. EATS HER EGGS
subject: cuckoo catfish
first_comment: If the catfish fry run out of cichlid eggs, they start eating each other. Would you rather be the catfish or the cichlid?
